_meta.purpose: Why each of a product's photographs was used or rejected as a render reference. product-views.json holds only the survivors, so the reasoning lived nowhere and every re-run repeated the work — including the mistakes.

vendorScrape.finding: comfortelfurniture.com holds no photographs the catalogue is missing. Verified by curl and by rendering the pages: data-large_image is the gallery's only real source, the thumbnails are client-side Underscore templates, and there is no variation-gallery JSON. Blake Merlot, Oakley and Cloud Waiting Sofa have one photo each; Harper has the same 14 we hold.
vendorScrape.implication: Do not write another scraper expecting more angles. 23 renderable products have a single photograph and always will. scripts/scrape-product-images.mjs is kept only to re-check if the vendor reshoots.

rules: The shell identifies a styling chair, not the base: Capital Base Aluminum ($70), Omega Round Base ($70) and hydraulics ($98) are separate SKUs, which is why one chair is photographed on four to eight bases.
Prefer one base family across a set so the render draws consistent copies; never mix black with gold when a consistent run exists.
Where a variant IS the product it is unforgiving - a black-basin wash unit must never be referenced by its white-basin photographs.
The hero need not be image 1. Four reception desks lead with a lifestyle shot.
Filenames lie: Harper #11 and #13 are both named Black-Pump and have different columns.

verdicts.reject: not the same physical piece, or carries no silhouette (close-up, lifestyle, swatch, part, logo)
